transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my eating has gotten really messed up. I stopped caring about tracking my food, and I’ve been skipping actual meals for days—mostly just coffee and protein bars. Then I noticed my clothes were getting loose, like they were hanging off me, and I hadn’t even realized it was happening.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not trying to lose weight or avoid gaining it. It’s more like I just haven’t been eating normally, and I didn’t really notice the weight coming off until my clothes felt loose.
Has there ever been a time when you were worried about gaining weight?
Not that I can really remember. I don’t think I’ve had times where I was especially worried about gaining weight. It’s just not something I’ve focused on much.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you couldn't stop?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve had that happen in a clear way—like eating a huge amount and feeling unable to stop. Nothing really stands out to me like that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Yeah, I think so. I didn’t weigh myself much, but my eating got really messed up. I stopped keeping track of food, skipped actual meals for days, and was mostly just having coffee and protein bars. Then my clothes started feeling loose, kind of hanging off me, before I really noticed I’d lost weight.
Has there ever been a point in your life when the idea of gaining weight frightened you?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember a time where gaining weight actually frightened me. That hasn’t really been the issue for me.
Do you feel like you have a lack of interest in food or is it more that you're just not thinking about eating?

It’s more that I just wasn’t thinking about eating. Like, I stopped caring about keeping track of meals, and then I’d go days without having real food—just coffee and protein bars. I didn’t really notice how bad it got until my clothes started fitting loose.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you think about eating a normal meal?
Not really anxious or upset, no. It’s not like a normal meal scares me. I just... wasn’t thinking about food much, and meals kind of fell off my radar.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle?
I’m male, so I don’t have a menstrual cycle.
Do you think your eating habits changed because of any concerns about your body shape?
No, I don’t think it was about my body shape. I wasn’t trying to lose weight or change how I looked. I just wasn’t really paying attention to eating.
Do you ever avoid eating because you think it might lead to gaining weight?

No, I wasn’t avoiding food because I thought I’d gain weight. It was more like I just stopped caring about eating properly. I’d skip actual meals for days and just have coffee or a protein bar, and then my clothes started feeling loose before I really even noticed.
Do you feel like your weight loss was unintentional?

Yeah, it was unintentional. I wasn’t trying to lose weight. My eating just kind of went off the rails—I stopped keeping track of food, skipped real meals for days, mostly had coffee or a protein bar, and then I noticed my clothes were hanging loose.
Do you think your eating habits changed because of any emotional issues or stress you've been experiencing?

Yeah, I think stress or whatever was going on emotionally probably played a part. I just stopped caring about tracking food or making meals. I’d go days without real meals, just coffee and protein bars, and then my clothes were hanging loose before I even really noticed.
Was there a specific stressful event or period that you think triggered your change in eating habits?

Yeah. It was after I got handed this temporary PMO-level responsibility at work. It didn’t happen overnight, but over maybe three weeks things just kind of built up, and that’s when my eating started slipping.
Do you ever feel like once you start eating, you might not be able to stop?

Not really. It’s more been the opposite — once my eating got off track, I’d just skip real meals for days and get by on coffee or a protein bar. I wasn’t trying to, I just stopped paying attention, and then my clothes started getting loose before I really noticed.
Do you worry that if you start eating a normal amount, you won't be able to control how much you eat?

No, I don’t really worry about overeating or losing control once I start. It’s more that my eating went completely off the rails the other way — I stopped caring about tracking anything, skipped actual meals for days, and just got by on coffee and protein bars. My clothes started hanging loose before I really even noticed.
Do you feel like you might lose control over how much you eat if you start eating normally again?

No, I don’t really feel like I’d lose control eating normally. The problem has been more that I just stopped paying attention to food at all — I quit tracking, skipped real meals for days, and was basically getting by on coffee and protein bars. My clothes started hanging loose before I even really noticed.
Have you ever felt afraid of gaining weight at any point in your life?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve cared how I look like most people, but I don’t remember being afraid of gaining weight or anything like that.
Do you think your eating habits would change if you gained back the weight you lost?

I don’t think gaining the weight back would really change the issue much. It wasn’t like I was eating less on purpose because of the weight. I just stopped caring about food tracking, skipped actual meals for days, and was mostly running on coffee and protein bars. The weight loss was more something I noticed after my clothes started getting loose.
